items.text: ALTERNATIVE METHOD ALTERNATIVE METHOD

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: We've doubled the second equation so that we can trace what happens to all the 2PbO from the first one.

items.label: text
items.text: This could also be simplified to 1 mol PbS produces 1 mol Pb. This would save you doing some arithmetic as you would not have to multiply everything by 2. However, in the end it does not make any difference to the answer, so you do not have to simplify it if you don't want to.

items.label: section_header
items.text: HINT

items.label: text
items.text: There are advantages and disadvantages of both methods. For the first method, we can use the same three steps in all the calculations we do below. However, a bit more maths will be involved: converting tonnes to grams and back again. The alternative method has fewer steps but we cannot use it in the same way when doing some of the calculations involving solutions in the next chapter.

items.label: section_header
items.text: WHAT IS A PERCENTAGE YIELD?

items.label: text
items.text: 2PbS(s) + 3O2(g) → 2PbO(s) + 2SO2(g)

items.label: text
items.text: PbO(s) + C(s) → Pb(I) + CO(g)

items.label: text
items.text: Interpret the equation in terms of moles and trace the lead through the equations: 2 mol PbS produces 2 mol PbO

items.label: text
items.text: If we double the second equation:

items.label: text
items.text: 2PbO(s) + 2C(s) → 2Pb(l) + 2CO(g)

items.label: text
items.text: we can see that 2 mol PbO produces 2 mol Pb.

items.label: text
items.text: In other words, every 2 mol of PbS produces 2 mol of Pb.

items.label: text
items.text: Substitute masses where relevant. In this case, the relevant masses are only the PbS and the Pb:

items.label: text
items.text: 2 × 239 g PbS produces 2 × 207 g Pb 478g PbS produces 414g Pb

items.label: text
items.text: Now there seems to be a problem. The question is asking about tonnes and not grams. You could calculate how many grams there are in a tonne. However, it's much easier to think a bit, and realise that the ratio is always going to be the same, whatever the units, which means that:

items.label: text
items.text: 478 tonnes PbS produces 414 tonnes Pb

items.label: text
items.text: Do the proportion calculation:

items.label: text
items.text: If 478 tonnes PbS produces 414 tonnes Pb

items.label: text
items.text: 417 then 1 tonne PbS gives tonne Pb = 0.866 tonne 478

items.label: text
items.text: 0.866 tonne of lead is produced from 1 tonne of galena.

items.label: section_header
items.text: CALCULATING PERCENTAGE YIELDS

items.label: text
items.text: If you calculate how much product a reaction might produce, in real life you rarely obtain as much as you expected. If you expect to get 100g, but only get 80 g, your percentage yield is 80%. The rest of it has been lost in some way. This could be due to spillages, or losses when you transfer a liquid from one container to another. Or it may be that there are all sorts of side reactions going on, so that some of your starting materials are changed into unwanted products. That happens a lot during reactions in organic chemistry.
